source_name: ECB — Instant Payments Regulation (IPR) implementation hub
why_relevant: Central reference for IPR application dates (reachability, sending, VoP, sanctions screening) that bind every euro-area PSP including all Slovenian banks. Directly drives SI vendor/procurement timelines.

source_name: ECB AMI-Pay / AMI-SeCo market group meeting documents
why_relevant: Meeting packs contain unusually candid deployment status updates (e.g. EPC's May 2026 VoP deployment presentation) months ahead of formal publication — an early-warning channel on payments-scheme readiness relevant to SI PSPs.

source_name: European Payments Council — Document library (rulebooks, incl. VoP Scheme Rulebook v1.1)
why_relevant: EPC scheme rulebooks (SCT, SCT Inst, SDD, VoP) are the operational rules Slovenian PSPs must implement to satisfy the IPR. Rulebook versions and effective dates are the concrete implementation deadlines behind the EU regulation.

source_name: European Payments Council — Public consultations on scheme rulebook change requests
why_relevant: EPC runs 3-month public consultations on change requests (e.g. the SCT Inst consultation open to 11 June 2026). These are the earliest visible signal of scheme changes SI banks will have to fund.

source_name: EPC — Register of Participants / scheme participant lists (Slovenian PSPs)
why_relevant: Shows which Slovenian PSPs have adhered to each EPC scheme, i.e. who is contractually bound and who is still to onboard — a concrete adoption-gap indicator for SI.

source_name: ESRB — Recommendations and Warnings
why_relevant: ESRB recommendations carry 'act or explain' obligations with fixed compliance deadlines for addressees including Slovenian authorities; they often precede binding national measures by 12-24 months.

source_name: EUR-Lex — Uradni list Evropske unije, serija L (daily view, Slovenian)
why_relevant: The Slovenian-language Official Journal is the authentic legal text binding in Slovenia. Publication in OJ L fixes entry-into-force and application dates for CRR3, PSD3/PSR, DORA, IPR and their delegated acts.

source_name: EUR-Lex — Slovenian legislation summaries and CELEX consolidated texts (payments/banking)
why_relevant: Consolidated SL texts and 'povzetki zakonodaje' give the Slovenian legal vocabulary (e.g. 'Uredba o enotnem območju plačil v eurih') used by Banka Slovenije and SI banks, and link each act to its implementing measures.

source_name: European Commission — Have your say (public consultations on EU financial services acts)
why_relevant: Level 1 consultations and delegated-act feedback periods for PSD3/PSR, FIDA, CRR3 amendments appear here with hard feedback deadlines, and are available in Slovenian. Earliest possible lead time in the EU pipeline.

source_name: Law-firm and consultancy EU regulatory trackers (Norton Rose 'Regulation Tomorrow', PwC Legal, KPMG, Morrison Foerster)
why_relevant: Fast, dated secondary summaries of EBA/ECB/Commission publications with implied timelines (PSD3/PSR expected in force late 2027, IPR milestones). Useful as a discovery tripwire and cross-check, never as primary evidence.

source_name: Bankart d.o.o. — Plačilni sistemi in storitve (payment systems & services)
why_relevant: Bankart is the central SI processor and operator of the BIPS / BIPS IP / SIMP-PS payment systems used by essentially every Slovenian bank and savings bank. This section is the operator's own description of the systems it runs and is the anchor page from which its scheme/participant documentation is published.

source_name: Bankart — Opis plačilnih sistemov za procesiranje SEPA transakcij (SL/EN, versioned PDF)
why_relevant: The closest public equivalent to a scheme/system rulebook: describes BIPS, BIPS IP (domestic SCT Inst), BIPS T (cross-border instant via TIPS) and SIMP-PS, participation eligibility, settlement and financial-risk arrangements. Republished under a dated filename, so version deltas expose operational and compliance changes for participants.

source_name: Bankart — Aktualno (operator news & participant notices)
why_relevant: Operator's own news channel; the natural place where scheme releases, migration milestones and Flik/BIPS changes are first announced to the SI market. Low volume, high signal-to-noise for operational deadlines.

source_name: Bankart — Flik Pay / Flik POS scheme-adjacent documentation (privacy rules, merchant onboarding, FAQ)
why_relevant: Flik is the SI national instant-payment scheme; the scheme rulebook itself is not public, but Bankart's Flik privacy rules, merchant onboarding manuals and FAQ explicitly reference 'pravila slovenske nacionalne sheme Flik' and carry versioned technical/operational requirements for PSPs and acquirers.

source_name: Banka Slovenije — Gradiva sej Nacionalnega sveta za plačila (NSP meeting materials & minutes)
why_relevant: Confirmed minutes of ~38 sessions (latest referenced April 2026). Minutes routinely record scheme-migration timetables, UPN/UPN QR standard changes and instant-payment rollout status months before they appear as binding participant deadlines. Highest-yield SI-specific forward-deadline source in this cell.

source_name: Banka Slovenije — Nadzor plačil in infrastruktur / pregled plačilnih in poravnalnih sistemov (oversight of payment & settlement systems)
why_relevant: Defines the reporting obligations imposed on payment system operators (upravljavci plačilnih sistemov) and the licensing regime under ZPlaSSIED. These are hard, dated compliance obligations for Bankart and any other SI system operator, and the reporting templates themselves reveal system scope.

source_name: Združenje bank Slovenije (ZBS) — Standardi (technical standards, incl. UPN QR)
why_relevant: ZBS is the standard-setting body for the UPN / UPN QR national payment order. The 'Tehnični standard Univerzalni plačilni nalog UPN QR' published here is the binding technical specification whose version changes force issuer, printer, bank and software-vendor migration deadlines across the whole SI market.

source_name: ZBS — SEPA section (scheme guidance, ISO 20022 XML manuals, UPN QR specs, SDD mandates)
why_relevant: The SI national SEPA adherence/implementation hub: ISO 20022 XML implementation manuals for SCT and SDD, UPN QR form specifications, SDD mandate templates. Effectively the national-migration body layer between EPC rulebooks and SI banks — where EPC rulebook release cycles get localised into SI participant obligations.

source_name: ZBS — news / obvestila on payment regulation implementation (Instant Payments Regulation, VoP)
why_relevant: ZBS publishes market-facing notices that state exactly when SI banks must have implemented scheme/regulatory changes (e.g. 9 October 2025 full instant-payment obligation and Verification of Payee, transitional period to 2027 for non-euro member states). These are the operational deadline announcements for the whole SI participant base.

source_name: UPN QR — upn-qr.si (technical standard, issuer/printer certification, programmer guidance)
why_relevant: The operational portal for the ZBS-UPN-QR standard: technical standard text, QR specification (Version 15, 77x77, byte mode, EC level M), programmer instructions, verification library and the registered-issuer process via UJP. Also carries governance notices — e.g. the ZBS Payment Transactions Committee decision to shut down the QR/print verification centre — which are exactly the kind of operational change invisible in supervisory channels.

source_name: UJP — Uprava Republike Slovenije za javna plačila: e-računi portal & issuer rules
why_relevant: UJP operates the public-sector e-invoicing rail and receives the 'Izjava o sprejemu pravil za izdajanje obrazca UPN' from registered UPN QR issuers. It also sets e-SLOG standard version cut-offs (e.g. e-SLOG 1.6/1.6.1 withdrawn 1 Oct 2020 in favour of 2.0) that are hard deadlines for banks, PSPs and ERP vendors.

source_name: Bankart — Register izdajateljev e-računov (SIMP e-invoice issuer register)
why_relevant: The operator-run register of e-invoice issuers on the SIMP rail. Registry-linked payment rail exactly as scoped by this cell: joining/leaving the register is an observable operational event, and the register's rules define participant obligations for banks and e-path providers.

source_name: Bankart d.o.o. — annual reports (Letno poročilo)
why_relevant: Operator annual reports narrate system launches, participant counts, volumes and forward project pipeline (e.g. BIPS IP go-live Feb 2019, Flik launch). Useful for reconstructing scheme timelines and for early sight of the next year's mandatory participant projects.

source_name: Nexi Slovenija d.o.o. (ex-NETS CEE, ex-Intesa Sanpaolo Card) — card processing operator
why_relevant: The second processing pole in SI alongside Bankart, and an NSP member. Registry/business-intelligence entries (Bizi, eBonitete, CompanyWall — the Dun & Bradstreet/ex-Bisnode-style layer) are the practical way to track corporate identity changes, ownership and legal-entity continuity of SI processing operators, which repeatedly rename.

source_name: Sistem Activa — multilateral card clearing system (Wikipedia SL entry as pointer)
why_relevant: Documents a second SI clearing rail: the Activa multilateral clearing system for card claims, operated by Banka Intesa Sanpaolo with daily settlement across TARGET2/T2 Slovenia accounts. Useful as an entry point to an actor easily missed when only Bankart is tracked; must be corroborated against Banka Slovenije's operator register.

source_name: Halcom — payment-software vendor release & upgrade notices (Hal E-Bank, MultiPay)
why_relevant: Halcom supplies the corporate e-banking rails used across SI banks. Its release notices are a high-fidelity leading indicator of scheme/regulatory deadlines because they name the exact cut-off date and the exact functional change (e.g. from 9 Oct 2025 older mBanka/MultiPay versions blocked; instant payments plus automatic recipient verification for SEPA payments). Vendor deadlines often surface before bank-side communication.

source_name: SI bank participant disclosures of scheme obligations (Flik / IPR general terms and notices)
why_relevant: Individual SI banks publish the participant-facing version of scheme rules — Flik general terms, IPR implementation notices, changed cut-off times. Because the Flik rulebook itself is not public, aggregating several banks' 'splošni pogoji' is the practical proxy for reconstructing scheme requirements and their effective dates.
